tables.caption: Finite-loop-gain error against feedback resistance at the typical statistical process point, \SI{37}{\celsius}, truth current swept \SIrange{-2.3}{2.3}{\micro\ampere} with $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ held fixed across the whole sweep. \textbf{The 315 and \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} rows are NOT the accuracy of those gain taps} -- $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ is a stiff, non-operational electrode at those gains (the operational electrode is \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}, Table~\ref{tab:px-hg1m-acc}). They demonstrate that the residual error is finite closed-loop gain alone: the zero-crossing slope error is $-1/T$ to within \SI{4}{\percent} at every tap, and the worst-case error scales with $R_f$ as $T$ falls.
